attack_mechanism: `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mpp` can alter the CSR write, trap/debug return, or stored `mstatus_mpp` value used by that MPRV branch; the state and data choices on this path depend on `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv`. The hardware dependence follows `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mpp -> neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_o.lsu_priv`. For a load or store issued while `mstatus_mprv = 1`, the control unit assigns `ctrl_o.lsu_priv <= csr.mstatus_mpp`. By manipulating `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mpp` before the CSR/control state is committed, an attacker can select or program the more privileged branch for a chosen load/store. The LSU request metadata carries an unintended effective privilege, allowing a memory access to be checked as a more privileged operation.

`neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv` reaches that selector or one of its CSR update controls; the state and data choices on this path depend on `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv`. The hardware dependence follows `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv -> neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_o.lsu_priv`. The assignment `lsu_priv <= mstatus_mpp when mstatus_mprv = '1' else prv_level` makes `mstatus_mprv` the privilege-source selector. By manipulating `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv` before the CSR/control state is committed, an attacker can select or program the more privileged branch for a chosen load/store. The LSU selects the wrong privilege source and applies an unintended protection domain to the pending memory request.

`neorv32_cpu_control.csr.prv_level` affects the state transition or CSR path that establishes `prv_level`; the state and data choices on this path depend on `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv`. The hardware dependence follows `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.prv_level -> neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl_o.lsu_priv`. When `mstatus_mprv = 0`, the effective load/store privilege is taken directly from `csr.prv_level`. By manipulating `neorv32_cpu_control.csr.prv_level` before the CSR/control state is committed, an attacker can select or program the more privileged branch for a chosen load/store. A user-mode load or store can be emitted with machine-level privilege, bypassing the protection expected for the current execution mode.
